reason: Introduces the leakage-adjusted simulatability (LAS) metric for whether a model's own NL explanations help an observer predict its outputs, and optimizes explanations for it. This is a core rationale-simulatability measurement.
title: Leakage-Adjusted Simulatability: Can Models Generate Non-Trivial Explanations of Their Behavior in Natural Language?
evidence: arXiv comment says EMNLP 2020 Findings. Semantic Scholar gives ACL Anthology id 2020.findings-emnlp.390 (pp. 4351-4367). Read the abstract.

reason: Adds a cross-model transfer reward to RLVR: a reasoning prefix is rewarded when a separate receiver model continues it to the correct answer. This is a rationale sufficiency and informativeness reward, and the paper measures prefix utility for held-out receivers. Borderline: there is no faithfulness evaluation.
title: Beyond Correctness: Learning Robust Reasoning via Transfer
evidence: arXiv v1 has no comment or journal_ref; Semantic Scholar says arXiv. The same title is an ICLR 2027 submission on OpenReview (forum 4VQacZlySN). Read the abstract and HTML.

reason: RL with a small-LLM consistency reward that penalizes rationales diverging from the final answer. It measures reasoning-answer consistency (+16.5%) and reports reward hacking by concealing reasoning, which a legible-format stage mitigates.
title: CLARity: Reasoning Consistency Alone Can Teach Reinforced Experts
evidence: Listed in the ACL Anthology as 2026.acl-long.1358. arXiv comment says ACL 2026 Main Conference; Semantic Scholar DBLP key is conf/acl/LinJWSF26. Read the HTML (Sec. 5.4, related work).

evidence: The arXiv abs page shows v3 (1 KB) withdrawn with the comment 'part of a different work'. Semantic Scholar says arXiv only. An arXiv author search found no successor.

evidence: Read the abstract and grepped the HTML: no faithfulness, legibility or monitoring hits. arXiv comment says Accepted at NeurIPS 2025, and Semantic Scholar agrees.

reason: Studies cross-model CoT transfer, i.e. how another model's trace prefixes help a receiver (answer leakage vs scaffolding), and explicitly says its findings are not evidence about faithfulness; it measures no faithfulness, monitorability or legibility property.

reason: Studies whether plausible explanations sway multimodal LLM judges, which is judge robustness. It does not measure whether the explanations faithfully reflect the generating model's reasoning.

reason: Borderline. It measures how far answers rely on and defer to the model's own reasoning trace (Lanham-style deletion, answer-swap corruption, cache masking) when the trace conflicts with evidence. It shows that deletion-based trace-use measures do not reveal which source the answer follows, which is a diagnostic of CoT-reliance measurement, although the framing is a knowledge conflict.
title: When Reasoning Traces Conflict with Evidence: How Answer Configuration Shapes Evidence Following
evidence: arXiv v2 comments give only the page count, and web search found no venue (Semantic Scholar was rate-limited). Read the abstract, the introduction, §5.3, §6 (positioned against faithfulness metrics) and Appendix E.
